Transliterate Text to Plain ASCII

Source: R/lib_helpers.R
toascii.Rd

Converts a character vector to plain 7-bit ASCII, transliterating accented or non-Latin characters to their nearest ASCII equivalent (for example, an accented capital A becomes a plain "A"). Falls back to dropping any character that has no transliteration. This is the deterministic "fallback" used by asciifb(). Use it for destinations that accept only ASCII – a package DESCRIPTION, a file name, a legacy system – so a name written with an accented letter arrives with the plain letter rather than as an encoding error or a question mark.

Usage

toascii(x)

Arguments

x

A character vector (other types are converted with as.character()).

Value

A character vector the length of x, containing only printable ASCII characters (bytes 32 to 126); NA elements become "".

Details

Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 at all (a mislabelled file) are dropped first. Then, when the stringi package is installed, the ICU transform "Any-Latin; Latin-ASCII" romanises any script and folds accents (Cyrillic, Greek and Chinese become Latin letters). Without stringi, a fixed table folds the common Latin accents and ligatures (sharp s to "ss", the ae ligature to "ae", thorn to "th" and so on) and every other non-ASCII character is dropped, so non-Latin scripts disappear rather than being romanised. Either way the result is then stripped of anything outside the printable ASCII range (space to tilde), so control characters such as newlines and tabs are removed too. The result never depends on the session's locale.

A missing value becomes ""; non-character input is converted with as.character() first (so numbers pass through as their digits).

See also

asciifb() to transliterate only when needed, wrtxtfb() to write text with an ASCII retry.

Examples

# Latin accents fold to their nearest ASCII letter.
toascii("Prof. \u00c1ngela Zorro Medina")  # "Prof. Angela Zorro Medina"
#> [1] "Prof. Angela Zorro Medina"

# Vectorised over the input.
toascii(c("Se\u00e1n", "Zo\u00eb", "na\u00efve"))
#> [1] "Sean"  "Zoe"   "naive"

# Non-Latin scripts are romanised when stringi is available.
if (requireNamespace("stringi", quietly = TRUE))
  toascii("\u041c\u043e\u0441\u043a\u0432\u0430")  # "Moskva" (Cyrillic)
#> [1] "Moskva"

# Either way the result is guaranteed pure 7-bit ASCII (never "?").
all(charToRaw(toascii("caf\u00e9")) < 128)
#> [1] TRUE

# Missing values become empty strings; line breaks are removed.
toascii(c(NA, "two\nlines"))
#> [1] ""         "twolines"
